facts.text: On this day in 1859, Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species' — all 1,250 first-edition copies sold out the same day.
On this day in 1963, Lee Harvey Oswald was shot live on American television, the first murder ever broadcast in real time.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than exist in the entire continent of Australia.
The Philippines is the only country in the world where divorce remains fully illegal for non-Muslim citizens.
Tokyo's greater metro area holds 37 million people — more than the entire population of Canada, compressed into one city.
On this day in 1954, the Dow Jones closed below 383 — the same level it had hit in 1929 before the crash. It took 25 years for American stocks to fully recover.
On this day in 1987, oil fell below $18 a barrel, capping a collapse of over 60% in under two years — a faster crash than the Great Depression wiped stocks.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded in 1792 under a buttonwood tree. The original 24 brokers agreed to charge each other fixed commissions, creating a cartel that lasted 183 years.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion — a world record — yet the company sold less than 2% of itself. It briefly became the first firm ever valued above $2 trillion.
The term 'bear market' likely predates Wall Street entirely, tracing to an 18th-century proverb about selling a bear's skin before catching the bear — a warning against speculation.
On this date in 1859, Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species'. The first edition of 1,250 copies sold out the same day.
On this date in 1974, Donald Johanson unearthed Lucy in Ethiopia. At 3.2 million years old, she walked upright long before the human brain began its dramatic expansion.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces roughly 3.8 million red blood cells every second. Each one lives about 120 days before the spleen quietly dismantles it.
Light takes 8 minutes to reach Earth from the Sun, but up to 100,000 years to travel from the Sun's core to its surface first.
On this day in 1859, Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species.' The entire first edition — 1,250 copies — sold out before noon.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The pyramid is that old.
On this day in 1963, Lee Harvey Oswald was shot live on American television, the first murder most viewers had ever watched in real time.
The fax machine was invented in 1843 — before the telephone, before the light bulb, 140 years before most offices actually got one.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. It was taking students before Mexico City existed.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved and gone. Linguists consider it untranslatable — English requires an entire sentence to approximate one Portuguese word.
Hiraeth (Welsh): homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. It carries grief, nostalgia, and yearning simultaneously — a feeling most languages leave nameless.
On this day in 1859, Darwin published On the Origin of Species. The word 'evolution' barely appears — Darwin preferred 'descent with modification', finding evolution too loaded.

Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the wordless look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The Yaghan language of Tierra del Fuego gave us our most efficient word for awkward desire.

On this day in 1963, Lee Harvey Oswald's killer Jack Ruby described his act as 'tsuris' — Yiddish for anguished trouble. A word borrowed from Hebrew tzarot quietly entered a presidential assassination transcript.

On this date in 2013, Bitcoin surpassed $1,000 for the first time on Mt. Gox — a milestone reached just four years after the genesis block mined a 50 BTC reward that can never be spent: Satoshi hard-coded it unspendable.

On Nov 24, 2017, Bitcoin Cash underwent its first scheduled difficulty adjustment — a direct consequence of its Emergency Difficulty Adjustment algorithm, which caused wild mining oscillations that briefly made BCH more profitable to mine than BTC.

Ethereum's gas limit is not set by the protocol — it is voted on block-by-block by miners (now validators), who can nudge it up or down by 1/1024th per block, making it a continuous soft referendum on network capacity.

The Bitcoin whitepaper uses the word 'chain' exactly once. The phrase 'blockchain' never appears in it — the term emerged organically in forum usage and was retroactively applied to Nakamoto's design.

Uniswap v2 launched with no admin keys, no pause function, and no upgrade path — meaning the $2B+ in liquidity it once held was governed entirely by immutable bytecode that no living person can alter.

On this date in 1997, IBM's Deep Blue team published their analysis of the May match where it defeated Kasparov — the first time a computer beat a reigning world chess champion under standard tournament conditions.

On this date in 2022, Galactica was pulled from public access after just three days. Meta's 120B-parameter scientific LLM confidently generated plausible-sounding but fabricated citations, exposing a core alignment problem before alignment was the dominant discourse.

GPT-4's training run is estimated to have cost over $100 million in compute alone — meaning the weights sitting on OpenAI's servers represent a capital expenditure comparable to a mid-sized particle physics experiment.

Transformers were not invented for language. The 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper targeted machine translation specifically; the architecture's dominance across vision, protein folding, and audio was entirely unplanned.

The first neural network to beat humans at ImageNet — AlexNet in 2012 — ran on two consumer GTX 580 GPUs with 3GB of VRAM each. Modern frontier vision models require clusters that would consume that card's entire memory budget per attention head.
